The UI/UX is a complete mess—feels like no thought was given to the flow of interactions. Default keybinds are Z, X, and the arrow keys… Weird as hell. Dialogues repeat endlessly, and after the first time, you just don’t care anymore. But nope, you’re forced to fast-forward through them every single time, which makes up 95% of the game. This gets frustrating fast and even leads to misclicks from sheer boredom. The story tries way too hard to be edgy, like it was written by some doomer who saw [i]Un Chien Andalou [/i] once—or just that one eyeball scene on YouTube—because, of course, there’s a weird reference to it in a cutscene featuring the dev’s webcam. On the "bright side", the RNG is decent. Even if you get unlucky too many times in a row, there’s usually still a way to pull through. But honestly, this could have been a much better roguelike if the overall flow of gameplay was improved.

太好玩了！！！！不枉demo等了这么久！！正式版Luna可以说是史诗版加强，demo真是没能让luna大人使出全力啊（扶额苦笑） ———————————— I really love how you can TALK to enemies in the game, which is available after you reach the third area. Always wondered what dialogue earlier enemies/bosses might have—thought I’d never see it until I realized [spoiler]Luna can respawn in earlier areas after dying, bringing TALK with her. Unfortunately, I only discovered this after defeating Angel III, so I missed out on some of the dialogues. I plan to replay the game to catch those. Also, you can chat with your friends in the first area, they’ll give you some useful tips![/spoiler] I’d say Luna is now one of my favorite characters (remember to buy the emergency dagger!). For the [spoiler]negative percentage[/spoiler] boss rush, The trick is to defend as much as possible until you figure out the boss’s attack patterns, then take advantage of their charging phase during the devastating attack. You just need patience. As a rogue-like game, I was really surprised by how much story it has, and there are even some puzzle elements![spoiler]There's also breaking the fourth wall and changes in game style???[/spoiler] Dream Diary has improved a lot compared to the demo, adding battles that require some strategy. Noire part...[spoiler]Yume Nikki reference?![/spoiler] Trish’s fight can be really frustrating, though, because of how random it is! Ideally, get Ambush and Dummy, save the Liquor Bottle for the final boss. Start by using the gun and then the bottle to avoid the poison effect. Even so, if you’re unlucky and keep missing, it might still lead to failure. The effects in the hallway are also luck-based... Hope this gets tweaked. Patience’s Dream Diary has way too much RNG… Has anyone else had four consecutive misses when attacking????? After an hour of RNG hell I quit the game. Can we just set weapon accuracy to 100% here?? Still have one last diary and [spoiler]Roma[/spoiler] to unlock, should be close. ———————————— ↑ 很喜欢你游的交谈功能，谁能想到我会这么喜欢一个肉鸽游戏的剧情。。？不精准的概括就是：很多谜语+toxic friends（？）非常好肉鸽和解谜使我4天玩了14h 梦日记，你还有什么惊喜是朕不知道的.jpg ———————————— 主游戏可以自选难度，不会影响剧情。如果不想挑战自我，建议玩标准Faith 1和简单难度（用月亮碎片买来解锁） Dream Diary模式会比较考验策略和规划 * 这模式里的攻击命中率可能会演你。。重灾区是Trish的和Patience的，前者好像已经优化了？后者……能玩到那里的人心态可能已经被捶打至Q弹爽滑了（。。）但还是想说攻击接连miss太搞心态了。。。随机数享受者狂喜（大嘘） 四十块钱买不了吃亏买不了上当，快来玩啊！！甚至国区只用25！

Here are my final thoughts. The game features a minimalistic graphic style and gameplay, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. The issue lies in its actual content. NoEye-Soft failed to grasp a concept, from beginning to end. The result is unsatisfying, as we just play through a series of nonsensical events. There isn't a proper story to tell, just a gigantic, useless, and incomprehensible self-indulgence. The dialogues between the characters are almost embarrassing. The gameplay quickly becomes repetitive. And not to mention breaking the fourth wall, which at this point is just breaking something else. Final score: 48 out of 100. /s a truly unexpected event. ;)

NO-SKIN felt incredibly repetitive. I understand how the difficulty and progression system works, but it doesn't do it any favors. A game doesn't become "more fun" when the challenge becomes "unlock increasingly annoying debuffs". If there was more of a story to it I'd be interested, but everything is so non-sequitur that it becomes a jumbled mess. Its not very expensive, which is a plus, but its just not really worth my time. It all feels sort of like a time sink, albeit a short one, and "upping the difficulty" with each Faith run doesn't seem to add anything to the game. There's a (sort of?" meta-progression system but the benefits are minute at best, destructive at worse. I feel like something is here, but its not something I enjoyed. Just couldn't really get into it despite giving it a solid hour and a half - most of the time I was spamming through things because it was the same rooms, same fights, same events. Even my strategy ended up feeling the exact same to win - get a new knife, run away from fights, mash attack. I'm sure I'd have to change it due to the "Difficulty" system, but, I don't want to because I don't find it very fun.

It's a confident game with good art and many nooks to it. I have two problems though. 1) It's not a roguelike, like it says in the description. All content is present every run -- like how the merchant frogs (the moon goddess have mercy on their souls) always have a set item list. The rooms all have the same loot. You can farm the non-random events. So you can choose your playstyle out in advance, and not have to react to randomness. It's like a puzzler RPG with permadeath -- which is fine in itself, but I feel a bit misled. 2) The game has some UI problems that slow you down. The game explains status effects EVERY TIME, requiring you to hit a button to advance. It's the same for talking and trading. Read the flavor text of the long-gilled fish? Get ready to skip past four text screens each time you want to buy something. For a game that is meant to be replayed and replayed, this really became tedious and made me not want to continue. Probably 1/2 my play time (literally) was pressing Z (odd default bindings) to advance. - In other ways, it's a cool game that draws on interesting inspirations. So don't feel put off from buying it as long as you know it's not really a roguelike, and aren't burnt out on tedious UI or display elements.

"Here are my final thoughts. The game features a minimalistic graphic style and gameplay, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. The issue lies in its actual content. NoEye-Soft failed to grasp a concept, from beginning to end. The result is unsatisfying, as we just play through a series of nonsensical events. There isn't a proper story to tell, just a gigantic, useless, and incomprehensible self-indulgence. The dialogues between the characters are almost embarrassing. The gameplay quickly becomes repetitive. And not to mention breaking the fourth wall, which at this point is just breaking something else. Final score: 48 out of 100." ... Hehe... I'm just playing with you... A truly unexpected event... This game has been something of a comfort game for me during a really hard period in my life, so I may be biased in its favor. Just thought I should put that out there. That said, I've found it compelling and addictive. It's satisfying as a roguelike, especially if you're the sort of person (like me) who looks for the best way to exploit and break the game--a certain secret specifically relies on doing that. The gameplay serves as the backdrop for a complicated interpersonal drama that you unravel piece by piece, which I'm still not totally sure I 100% understand, but I know I haven't seen all the content in the game yet, either. The themes are very grim and gritty, which is very much to my taste. In order to unlock some things, there is a separate game mode that is much more of a puzzle game than a roguelike, and it tickles the part of my brain that loves to try to "solve" combat like a puzzle in the base game. It also turns your expectations on their head and each of the memory segments has impressed me in some way. The music is soft and moody and enhances the gameplay. The biggest draw in this game, imo, is the secret-hunting. There's always something more to unravel, and it's good about giving you just the right amount of guidance to find something new. Every time I think I've got this game all figured out, it teases me with the next discovery. It is going to require some patience, but if you typically like roguelikes, this should not be difficult for you. Most of the progression comes in the form of learning the game's ins and outs, rather than unlocking straight mechanical upgrades; you mostly unlock new opportunities for the chance for something good in future runs. I'd recommend this game. Maybe not to everybody, but definitely if you like roguelikes and psychological dread and very dark themes. This game's got heart. And blood.

超现实恐怖风格的回合制肉鸽，机制不深但是可玩性一流。 战斗系统比较简约。双方数值都不高，所以资源管理才是要点，压战损尽快解决战斗才可以留足后路。机制少所以不算有什么战斗流派分支，但难度也不可小觑。 重复游玩度不错。五个人物，多种结局，局外成长，进阶制难度，足以翻来覆去玩好多遍。 个人最爱的特点，就是秘密超多。类似《邪恶冥刻》一样，一路向前并没有办法通关，只有做出局外解谜才能顺利推进度，每个人物都有独特的结局路线。战斗内也有很多隐藏机制有待发现：并非无用的道具，可招募队友，一招必杀boss，只能说知识就是力量...... 叙述风格挺酷的，很能整活，真结局之前我完全不理解情况hhh 缺点就是有时太看脸。比如说进商店有概率遇陷阱，不巧就是强制无收益吃战损。低难度就认了，难度高了就给人强烈的SL欲。

[quote]"You're dead. Your friends are dead. Your family is dead. Your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pets are being skinned alive. Your mom's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥. You suck at life. The whole world hates you. You're going to Hell. Live with it. Game Over."[/quote] NO-SKIN is a psychotic urban punk fairytale that plays like World of Horror if it was made by Daniel Mullins high off the Draft of Darkness' kitchen sink residue. I'm not flaunting the verbiage here, it's exactly as bizarre as it sounds. Be wary that this game bathes in gore and self-harm. If you aren't ready, you might find it getting under your skin upsetting. Now, it all begins with a group of friends discussing relatable topics like long shifts and lousy management. The friendliness ends soon after as the world goes dark. Your name is Noire and you drank too much, now you see a flayed man standing in the dark hallway on stubs for legs. He asks you where his skin is and demands it back. "Until you do, I will show you things as they really are." This is not a gift. Your apartment becomes a death trap, but don't despair. The Moon Goddess shall lend you a hand by bestowing her blessings and bringing you back to life. It's a roguelite, after all. The game immediately tells you that each action ends your turn except for items in your bag, which you can use to your heart's content, stacking up buffs. It does so to emphasise that consumables can do just about anything, so be resourceful, hoard, watch your only stat - hp. Weapons have 2 stats: damage and accuracy. By default, a knife is weak, yet a gun needs ammo. Both can be modified in unconventional ways. Having all that resource management in mind, you pick between rooms to enter. Each presents you with a list of events that could happen, their probabilities on display. Agency is king, make it count. On entering a room, you roll for an event and make even more choices. Partake in turned-based JRPG-like combat with clearly stated intents, kill to loot items as well as two types of currency that allows you to buy items from frogs and fish or recall memories for meta-progression upon death. When you don't fight, you solve surreal conundrums. Help the hanged man at the expense of some health? Play Russian roulette with a skeleton? You could talk to monsters, propose a trade, even hire one like it's Megami Tensei! Soon, you'll find out the intricacies of your bitter relations with your condemnatory frenemies. Nothing is as simple as it seems, there's a subtle questing system in place. But let's not dwell on something you'd rather discover for yourself. Action by action, you obtain a percentage of finding the skin, your Golden Fleece and a carrot on a stick. No-skin Man's curse intensifies as you progress no matter what you do, making your enemies stronger and your memories more vivid. Thus, you unlock more and more rooms to visit, muster an arsenal of items and perks, then pass thresholds, going deeper to face nasty bosses who sometimes cheat. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3464603841 Are you tripping? Is it a prank or a nightmarish delusion that forces you to murder your friends for real? Their caustic visages deteriorate alongside your glitching world. You constantly learn about them and the game, which never ceased to entice me with its raw emotion. Is it a story about human bonds? Penitence? A hard life? The throughline stitching its threads together is elusive. I won't tell you what's going on since the intrigue stemming from a simple premise is the bait. Besides, it would merely be my interpretation, not something certain. What I can tell is that this isn't a disposable kind of deal. It's too mental to get stale ahead of time. You'll unlock difficulties, characters with different agendas, and side-puzzles of the Dream Diary, expanding your knowledge and meta. When you think you broke the code, the labyrinth of suffering keeps growing with each beating like a bruise. At that, the game can be grindy and could use a fast-forward button for the repeated text. But it's a fun affair regardless. With clever mechanics to wrap your head around while taking wrapper after wrapper off this sour candy. It's cruelly hard, too, but offers an easy mode. Almost no strings attached. So, be not afraid, NO-SKIN was designed to appeal to a wider audience without losing its punk edge. This game earns its grit. First, it catches your eye, then slowly burrows into your brain. My curator [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35305390-Big-Bad-Mutuh/?appid=262060]Big Bad Mutuh[/url]

If I could only use one word to describe this game it would be disappointing. Personal opinion I don't understand how this game has as many glowing reviews as it does, I'm a sucker for randomness in games when it's deterministic in such a way that I know I can potentially get x outcome when I do y thing. This game takes that to its most logical extreme and it just becomes an exercise in frustration on higher lunar levels (this games version of ascensions). That being said, visually the game is unique; the story just seems like some edgy corner-of-the-internet humor. Maybe it does say something profound but I couldn't care less about 'lore' in videogames; I'd rather just read a book. Gameplay critique At first I was really into it, now I don't know if this is purposely done but my first run took me about 2 hours (the steam no questions asked refund window is 2 hours), taking my time doing the interactions just to get to the final fight and lose not realising what was to come. No big deal, get back to the fight a second time and I lose because I find out there's no rest; it's a boss gauntlet after the triplets. Again, no big deal lets just get back a third time. Oh I was on a run that was rocking melee? silly me I should of spread my stats better, my mistake game. Four attempts was how many it took to get a win, at no point after the first were any of the interactions meaningful. The text repeats so unless I missed something (Which to the games credit I may have) I don't get why I'd constantly talk to someone, it's unnecessary extra clicks. Why did my victory feel so unfulfilling??? I felt like I wasn't making choices, the game was deciding if it wanted me to do something and I just rolled with it almost like a damned if you do, damned if you don't scenario. What I mean by that is, lets say you want an item from the shop but you have no money? Ok; choose to go to rooms that have encounters to generate money right? Well you could hit the chance of getting that encounter with nothing there? Alright wasted a turn and the game moved on; great. Finally get your cash to spend but you need a shop? Alright lets go to the room with a shop; oh I kept getting the garbage event that does nothing for me wasting more time? Guess what I need to heal; I know I need to heal so lets go there. No you just hit the fight that you can't win so you have to waste attempts escaping losing more health... The game also features 'meta-progression' if you want to call it that, it's just mainly a few unlocks that after my limited playtime I had everything in the shop so why bother having it like that to begin with? I don't know. I believe the currency you use for the progression can be traded to npcs to ask for heals or items if you want to do that mid-combat, but again you're just prolonging encounters and the process has way too many sub-menus to bother; did anyone QA test this? no one said: "Hey after the first time doing this in an encounter we should speed this up for that one encounter??" Closing thoughts I'm not making this review to mock the game or bad mouth it, more of a warning to people who may be like me and saw the game and were interested in a turn based roguelike rpg; stay away. This isn't for me and it might not be for you either, it's basically just CBT at the end of the day.

NO-SKIN is a beautifully crafted and experimental psychological horror experience that... I'm...sorry dear reader I just want you to know that you absolutely disgust me. You should cut your own face off and swallow a razor blade or two. Was that unexpected? This entire game was unexpected! It's a wonderful slice of Rogue-Like that I never knew I needed. It's unassuming at first, but boy does it unravel more and more. Story? THE MOON IS FALLING AND YOU BETTER HURRY UP! ...But maybe after a few drinks first. And after a bit of trial and error error error error. The game-play is fairly simple to learn. It's a turn-based, choose your own route, and pray that your roommate doesn't shoot you type deal. The smallest decisions and outcomes make quite the difference as you try to weasel your way to the end. As you play you begin to unlock more options to help you please the Moon Goddess. New side stories are unlocked allowing you to access and obtain new items and characters such as <redacted> and <redacted>. You'll find yourself encountering something new each run and it's a joy to piece together this game more and more. I can't tell you how that body ended up in the kitchen officer, but I can tell you that this is a hidden gem of an indie. Well worth a try if you happen across it. You can tell the developer had a lot of fun making this game and I had a lot of fun playing it. Good luck making it across that hallway.

"Horror" game made by someone that has never been given a reason to actually be afraid, with every unfunny game dev gimmick that you could think of being summoned up. Not just "tacky 4th wall breaking", but LITERALLY everything you can think of. If I wanted to be reductive I'd just call this a "byproduct of the damage that toby fox has caused". Anything other than that, everything else has been self-reviewed by the author with his self-insert that you get to meet, though he seems to omit a lot of what makes the game actually jarring: https://youtu.be/zYHs1K5RY0Y I gave the game the genuine benefit of the doubt for 5 hours and I'm satisfied with not knowing anymore about it. Also, shoehorning meta progression and funlockables is not a necessary, helpful OR enjoyable addition to a """"""""rogue"""""""" """"""""""""like""""""""""""", if you can believe it. -- Edit -- I don't like comparing any media to it, but a friend called this a "yiiklike" and the shoe fits REALLY well.

I've had more than enough of those frustrating and RNG-dependent roguelites that demand me to go through exactly the same content innumerable times just to reach the end of the story. As a grown-ass adult, I don't have the time to waste with such nonsense, so this is likely going to be one more game in my library that I'll probably never finish. It's a shame, though. The general atmosphere, the lore and the story are interesting, I just can't be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with meaningless repetition anymore

Calling this game a rogue-lite is a stretch. Hell even calling it a game is a stretch as you'll be doing the same thing every time with nothing changing. The story is vague and uninteresting. The gameplay is simply go to room and fight enemies who are barely any different doing the same 2 moves over and over again. There's horror elements but calling this a horror game feels misleading. You want scares? You want dread? Wrong game, keep looking. Do you want to be bored out of your mind? This is the game for you. In my opinion this would go much further as a free game since even $7 feels too expensive for what we're given.

I am completely baffled by the high reviews for this. I was expecting a well-made horror roguelike in the same vein as Brutal Orchestra, but No Skin just completely fails at all aspects. The combat is tedious and incredibly simplistic. You have a knife that does 1 damage and a gun with limited ammo that does 2 damage. And it doesn't get much deeper than that. The relics are incredibly boring, with abilities like "restore 1HP after battle," or "do 1 damage extra on your first attack each battle." As a consequence, No Skin does not have anything resembling "builds." Instead, it's a game all about consumable item management, since you can use an unlimited number of items each turn. You can choose what enemy to fight next and they will generally drop the same items each time, so most of the so-called "strategy" is just fighting the correct enemy so that (for example), you'll have antidotes if big poison gets dropped on you. The fights are very short, but also super tedious because you do the same ones over and over. The aesthetic is arguably decent, but the writing is just terrible. I've cleared several runs and nothing resembling a "plot" has taken shape. All of the dialogue and narration reads like it was written by a 12-year-old girl, but not the talented tortured artist type. It's just a low IQ failed attempt to be "artsy" and "mysterious" with no actual substance behind it. If you are considering this game due to other reviews praising the story and writing, I strongly urge you to reconsider. It's a zoomerslop meme-game and incredibly overrated.

NO-SKIN feels like a Frankenstein's monster of "edgy" and "mysterious" indie horror games, and as someone who generally still appreciates the artistry and boundary-pushing of those games (even when they miss the mark), I unfortunately do not mean that as a good thing. My biggest issue with NO-SKIN is that it feels far too directionless; it's edgy for the sake of being edgy, and it's mysterious for the sake of being mysterious. This may not be the creator's intent, and I'm sure there is substance and underlying plot behind everything, but such a drip feed of actual narrative is provided that it ultimately feels purposeless. I can prattle on for a bit on why this is, but let's first focus on the fact that we are immediately thrown into the Horror™. Before we even get a proper backstory or reason to care about the cast of characters at the beginning (who all make poor first impressions, by the way), we are just thrust straight into the fray. NOW, this is not inherently an issue by itself. It is a Roguelike after all, and having a long introductory cutscene or section would not work well either IMO. Also, other excellent games like Signalis and Silent Hill more or less do the same thing. The DIFFERENCE, is that those games give us far more to work with as the player progresses, and we are eventually given reason to care about the cast and also far more context on why the world is the way it is. With NO-SKIN, even after almost 6 hours and beating the game multiple times (with nearly every run feeling nigh identical, even when factoring meta-progression and different playable characters), I still haven't the faintest clue about why I should give a damn about any of the side chars or Noire. I also finished all of the Dream Diaries up to Trish, and I still feel as if I know as much about Noire's "friends" as I did when I started my very first run. I finally gave in and decided to look at spoilers about the characters and all the endings, and I'm afraid to say that I neither care nor am able to empathize with literally anyone. And going back to my description of this game being a Frankenstein's monster, the world-building of this game does genuinely feel like that. It's an eldritch Lovecraft game where reality is an illusion, and the gods are inimical to humanity. It's also a meta-horror game where the video game is "aware" and the developer hates you!!! Also it's a psychological game about disastrous interpersonal relationships. Also there's dimensional hopping and alternate timeline stuff, and also it's Yume Nikki because everything might just be a dream, but also it isn't at all! And there's a bunch of quirky, Undertale-esque creatures to tie it all together!! Don't get me wrong, you can combine these concepts and create something that is both unique and memorable, but that still requires stable through lines that the narrative, on the surface, fundamentally lacks. And it is exponentially harder to weave these concepts together the more and more you stack on. If I seem way too harsh in this review, I apologise, but part of why I am such is because I do see genuine potential both in this game and the abilities of the developer. To list the good things, I think the art-style is evocative; it's the main reason why I bought the game in the first place. I think the game-play was engaging - it's very simple at first (not a bad thing) and gets quite repetitive as runs pass, but with some more work and variation, it could stand on its own. Combat as both a puzzle and as a narrative tool is peak, and works especially well for turn-based Survival Horror. Also, I'm a massive sucker for religious horror and religious motifs in art, so that's a plus. In summary, 2.5/5, I'll probably still end up copping Edenwound if / when it comes out since I do again see great potential, so hey, that's a win I suppose.

This is not a complete review since I decided to stop playing the game after 1.5 hour. I know me giving a downvote will not affect the overall score of the game on steam. It’s something I appreciate because my intention is not to harm the developer, but to make it clear what you’re in for if you’re not sure. The game has overwhelmingly positive which could imply that it will be enjoyed by practically everyone who plays it and that’s the part I want to push back against a little. So right off the bat, the game has an interesting presentation. The pixel graphics are expressive, the game intrigues with its set-up, I love the turn based combat and I don’t mind unraveling the story with little pieces here and there. But the game throws you in the midst of it, it feels like it wants to be mysterious for the sake of it. Now I don’t mind all of the aforementioned if the gameplay was engaging enough. That’s where it loses me. It’s described as roguelike but it doesn’t feel like one. It feels like the game is repurposed to become a roguelike with the small amount of content it has. It’s hard to explain why the activities it has feel very repetitive compared to other roguelikes, but you enter the same rooms, do the same fights, use the items and get the same temporary power ups multiple times on the same run. I feared this would be the case before playing the game but I went against my instincts since it’s part of a bundle I got and it was the last game in the list. I was right, the repetitiveness is worse than I thought. And you’re supposed to play the game many more times on higher difficulties if you want to get all the 4 achievements. I’m sorry to say but it doesn’t seem like the game has enough juice to justify that kind of investment. The audience that I can see loving the game are the ones who are drawn to the weird style it has by default, they want to look into what NPCs mean when they say unclear things, want to make connections and theorise about the story, want to discover secrets etc. The gameplay is barely serviceable but not strong enough to hold the game together on its own and it’s certainly not enough to be played many times, something that weights more heavily for the genre. Personally, I think it would have been better if the game was a short and traditional RPG with a couple of different endings. But hey, I’m clearly in the minority. Just make sure you get it for the reasons I mentioned instead of thinking you’re getting a traditional roguelike that remains fresh for a long time.

======== FULL REVIEW AFTER THE GRADING ======= Art: 9/10 (I love the body-horror aspects and no sprite seems to feel out of place!) Story: 8/10 Gameplay: 7/10 Pacing: 7/10 (It's amazing until it gets close to the end, also why I had to type a full review under this.) OVERALL: Casual: 8.5/10! Completionist: 5/10. ======== FULL REVIEW ======== I really loved this game up to a certain point, in fact it's what made me push to try and complete it fully, but it's just straight up ridiculous after some point. The start of the game is amazing, the random chance on each encounter makes each run feel interesting as you'll have to account for the possibilities of each room. The story is very captivating as you are barely introduced to it and have to learn more by playing, be it by risking your run to try a different path or just having to solve puzzles on another game mode. Aaaaannd that's where the game dies for me. After the first few puzzles (Which I really enjoyed!) the game decides to introduce RNG to the next ones and, if you want more content on the main gamemode, you gotta solve them. There's something truly hellish to finally understanding what you're supposed to do, then losing the next 6 attempts due to your character simply missing their attack, making you have to manually lose because of a single damage difference (since they don't have a quick restart, in fact you WILL be reading a bunch of dialogue on each retry) which is quite obviously not the nicest experience, even more when it doesn't happen for only one or two puzzles. But that is what I said I pushed through because of how much I loved this game and how much I wanted to leave a good review, since after progressing all the way to the very end, I was now made aware that (Trust me, not really a spoiler) you will need to replay 9 times on increasing difficulties without any differing progression whatsoever to finally get the actual final 100% completion ending... Which honestly, I am not sure I am willing to do, even more after seeing others complain about how enemies lose all the strategy aspects (Like waiting between moves to allow setup) and become a raw damage RNG battle on the later difficulties. Overall amazing game if you're not looking to get the full endings and such.

Roguelites need to be extremely well balanced, and I just find this one to be plain frustrating. It feels like way too much is out of my control; it's mostly RNG. I've gotten to the final stage 3 times, once all the way to the No-Skin man and literally beat him twice against all odds, but I didn't have his skin...which I though I would immediately get/find because the game implies you need to just get to 100% of the course to get it, so because he just kept reviving.. okay bud, maybe succum to infection or something lol Runs are basically based exclusively on luck and not on skill; start hoping you get good options for the blessings or else you might as well give up. Not that I am all that skilled but I've played other roguelites that also heavily rely on external blessings that haven't felt frustrating at any point. The blessings are just not balanced: some are really good and others are virtually useless, specially late game. Also, fatigue is actually one of the most frustrating mechanics I have ever faced in any games. I feel like it can probably soft block you at some point honestly. The art is cool and I personally enjoy this dark type of aspect of things but once random characters that seemingly have nothing to do with Noire start showing up it kind of ruined it for me. I don't know why this medival lady is here, and worse, I do not care to know. I'm not sure what's going on in general, and the dark edgy aesthetics can only carry me for 4 hours apparently. Unfortunately I think part of the problem is the extremely simple approach to game play. The game loops is Choose room > Hope for the best > Choose btwn attack/item/defend/escape (later a couple more options are added)> repeat. It's quick but also soooo luck based and gets boring fast. It just feels like a good basis to what could be a good game. But this is the full game. I'll give it an extra point because I'm pretty sure lesbians are involved...I'm pretty sure anyway

For a roguelite, it has a slow and difficult start, and initially there isn't a lot of feedback as to when or how you get permanent upgrades between runs. You may get the impression that it's construction is lazy or it's difficulty and obfuscation is needless. If you stick with it, there is a strict design language, and you will experience mastery of the mechanics and deeply satisfying discoveries. As soon as you rise above the challenge there will be more to scratch the itch, as well as easier routes to god builds where you can still be progressing universal unlocks. There is a very cheesy yet fun cakewalk if you want it, and there is constant gradual challenge if you want it too, and I felt like every really good new bit had just enough challenge without frustration - but be prepared that the first few runs is one of those challenges. There are multiple playable characters, multiple endings, frog fractions-esque genre divergences and core mechanics can be completely upended and branch into a ludicrous amount of content with so many interactions that it must of taken ages to plan and execute. Eventually, what you once suspected might be sparse and derivative will suddenly dawn on you as too big and too thought-out to be the pixel graphic indie horror dime a dozen genre clone you might be dreading. I was hoping for World Of Horror and hoping I would NOT get Undertale, and it's far more the former, but a wholly unique thing. NoEye-Soft's design philosophy and vision is extremely distinct, but also extremely measured and considered rpg strategy design. Mechanics, lore, and the meaning of the game and it's inception take meta turns. Some people just will never like that kind of thing, but I thought it was fascinating, rewarding, and a weirdly personal and moving glimpse into an artist's process of creating. Like a painting that shows you, through curiosity, effort and surprise - how it was made, why it was made, but still doing it's job of being beautiful and thought-evoking. The value for time makes this a no-brainer to pick up. The craftsmanship as a game, where there is puzzles and gameplay nested into places you wouldn't expect, make it exceptional for any price.

The art is beautiful, the way the game encapsulates the feeling of, and I'm not kidding, living in an undergraduate dorm, despite being a game about an eldritch monster placing a curse on you, is unmatched. Maybe I'm just projecting here, but I can't really describe this game any better than that. The horror is a mixed bag, aside from the art and the setting, in my hour the game didn't do anything to particularly "scare" you, but what do you call the genre of a man with no skin? I will come back to this review when I progress further, but my enjoyment is enough to leave a positive mark on the hour I did play.
